title: Job Chapter 40 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Job chapter 40 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Job Chapter 40 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Job Chapter 40.

questions.question: In Job 40, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Job laid his hand upon his mouth
The LORD spoke out of the whirlwind
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD answered Job
questions.explanation: This appears first in the chapter as stated in Job 40:1.

questions.question: Who answered Job in Job 40?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD answered Job, as found in Job 40:1.

questions.question: What does the LORD ask Job in Job 40:2?
options: Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him?
Wilt thou also disannul my judgment?
Gird up thy loins now like a man.
questions.correctAnswer: Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him?
questions.explanation: This question is posed by the LORD in Job 40:2.

questions.question: How does Job respond to the LORD in Job 40:3?
options: I will lay mine hand upon my mouth
questions.correctAnswer: I will lay mine hand upon my mouth
questions.explanation: Job expresses his response by stating he will lay his hand upon his mouth in Job 40:4.

questions.question: How many times does Job mention he has spoken in Job 40:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Twice
questions.explanation: Job states he has spoken once and twice in Job 40:5.

questions.question: From where did the LORD answer Job?
questions.correctAnswer: Out of the whirlwind
questions.explanation: The LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind as noted in Job 40:6.

questions.question: What does the LORD command Job to do in Job 40:7?
options: Gird up thy loins now like a man
questions.correctAnswer: Gird up thy loins now like a man
questions.explanation: The LORD instructs Job to gird up his loins like a man in Job 40:7.

questions.question: What does the LORD challenge Job about in Job 40:8?
questions.correctAnswer: To disannul His judgment
questions.explanation: The LORD asks Job if he will disannul His judgment in Job 40:8.

questions.question: What does Job say about himself in Job 40:4?
questions.correctAnswer: I am vile
questions.explanation: Job states, 'Behold, I am vile' in Job 40:4.

questions.question: In Job 40:5, what does Job say he will not do?
questions.correctAnswer: Answer
questions.explanation: Job declares that he will not answer in Job 40:5.

questions.question: What does Job intend to do after speaking twice according to Job 40:5?
options: Lay his hand upon his mouth
questions.correctAnswer: Lay his hand upon his mouth
questions.explanation: Job intends to lay his hand upon his mouth after speaking twice in Job 40:5.

questions.question: The LORD's address to Job was meant to demand something from him. True or False?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The LORD demands of Job in Job 40:7.

questions.question: Job acknowledges his lowly state in his response to the LORD. True or False?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Job acknowledges he is vile in Job 40:4.

questions.question: Job claims he has spoken three times in the chapter. True or False?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Job states he has spoken once and twice, not three times, in Job 40:5.

questions.question: The LORD asks Job if he will disannul His mercy. True or False?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The LORD asks Job if he will disannul His judgment, not His mercy, in Job 40:8.

medium.title: Job Chapter 40 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Job Chapter 40 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Job 40:9, what ability is questioned in comparison to God's power?
options: Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?
Canst thou create the heavens and the earth?
Canst thou command the morning and cause the dawn to know its place?
Canst thou make the stars shine brighter than the sun?
questions.correctAnswer: Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?
questions.explanation: Job 40:9 explicitly questions if one has an arm like God or can thunder with a voice like Him, highlighting God's unmatched power.

questions.question: What does Job 40:11 promise will happen if someone casts abroad the rage of their wrath as commanded in Job 40:10?
options: Every one that is proud will be abased.
The earth will open and swallow them.
They will be lifted up to the heavens.
They will receive great wealth and honor.
questions.correctAnswer: Every one that is proud will be abased.
questions.explanation: Job 40:11 states that casting abroad the rage of wrath results in beholding every proud person and abasing them, directly following the command to deck oneself with majesty in Job 40:10.

questions.question: In Job 40:15, what is the diet of the behemoth described as?
options: He eateth grass as an ox.
He feeds on fish by the river.
He eats fruits from the trees.
questions.correctAnswer: He eateth grass as an ox.
questions.explanation: Job 40:15 clearly states that behemoth eats grass like an ox, emphasizing its herbivorous nature.

questions.question: What is the connection between Job 40:12 and Job 40:13 regarding the treatment of the proud and wicked?
options: They are to be brought low, trodden down, hidden in dust, and bound in secret.
They are to be exalted and praised publicly.
They are forgiven and shown mercy.
They are to be given riches and honor.
questions.correctAnswer: They are to be brought low, trodden down, hidden in dust, and bound in secret.
questions.explanation: Job 40:12 and Job 40:13 together describe how the proud and wicked are to be humbled, trodden down, hidden in dust, and bound in secret, showing a progression of judgment.

questions.question: What practical lesson can Christians learn from the call to 'Deck thyself now with majesty and excellency' in Job 40:10?
options: To pursue righteousness and live with dignity reflecting God's glory.
To seek material wealth and social status.
To judge others harshly and without mercy.
questions.correctAnswer: To pursue righteousness and live with dignity reflecting God's glory.
questions.explanation: Job 40:10's call to array oneself with majesty and glory encourages living a life that reflects God's excellence and righteousness practically.

questions.question: How does Job 40:14 link personal salvation to the demonstration of power described in earlier verses?
options: Confession is made if one’s own right hand can save.
questions.correctAnswer: Confession is made if one’s own right hand can save.
questions.explanation: Job 40:14 states that God will confess to a person if their own right hand can save them, emphasizing reliance on divine power rather than self.

questions.question: According to Job 40:16, where is the behemoth’s strength especially located?
options: In his loins and the navel of his belly.
questions.correctAnswer: In his loins and the navel of his belly.
questions.explanation: Job 40:16 explicitly states that the behemoth’s strength is in his loins and the navel of his belly, emphasizing its physical power.

questions.question: What attitude toward the proud does God command in Job 40:11-12 and how should it be applied practically?
options: To abase and bring them low, applying humility and justice.
To praise them for their confidence.
questions.correctAnswer: To abase and bring them low, applying humility and justice.
questions.explanation: Job 40:11-12 commands abasing the proud and bringing them low, teaching believers to practice humility and uphold justice.

questions.question: How does Job 40:9 challenge believers regarding their faith and relationship with God?
options: By reminding them that no human can match God's power, encouraging trust in Him.
By telling them to rely solely on their own strength.
By instructing them to speak loudly like God.
By suggesting they can control nature.
questions.correctAnswer: By reminding them that no human can match God's power, encouraging trust in Him.
questions.explanation: Job 40:9 questions if anyone has God's power, underscoring the need for trust and faith in God's sovereignty.

questions.question: What does the description of the behemoth in Job 40:15-16 teach about God's creative power?
options: God’s creation is mighty, strong, and beyond human control.
God only creates small and weak animals.
Creation is unimportant compared to human power.
Behemoth is a mythical creature with no real significance.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s creation is mighty, strong, and beyond human control.
questions.explanation: Job 40:15-16 describes the behemoth as powerful and strong, illustrating God’s unmatched creative power.

questions.question: How might Job 40:14's statement about salvation impact a believer's understanding of self-reliance?
options: It discourages self-reliance and encourages dependence on God’s power.
It promotes complete self-reliance without God.
It suggests salvation depends on wealth.
It claims salvation is automatic regardless of actions.
questions.correctAnswer: It discourages self-reliance and encourages dependence on God’s power.
questions.explanation: Job 40:14 states that God will confess if the right hand can save, implying human power alone cannot save, promoting reliance on God.

questions.question: What practical application does Job 40:11’s call to 'Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath' have for Christian discipline?
options: It suggests righteous anger should be directed against pride and wickedness.
It encourages uncontrolled anger against all people.
It promotes revenge for personal offenses.
questions.correctAnswer: It suggests righteous anger should be directed against pride and wickedness.
questions.explanation: Job 40:11’s command encourages the use of righteous anger to address pride and wickedness, aligning with Christian discipline against sin.

questions.question: How do Job 40:12-13 describe the ultimate fate of the wicked, and what does this imply for believers’ view of justice?
options: They will be humbled, hidden, and bound, implying God’s justice is thorough and certain.
They will be exalted and celebrated.
They will be ignored by God.
They will be forgiven without repentance.
questions.correctAnswer: They will be humbled, hidden, and bound, implying God’s justice is thorough and certain.
questions.explanation: Job 40:12-13 describe the wicked being brought low and hidden, teaching believers that God’s justice is comprehensive and assured.

questions.question: According to Job 40:15, what does the creation of the behemoth alongside humans suggest about God's design?
options: God made powerful creatures to coexist with humans.
God created animals only for human use.
Behemoth is a symbol of human pride.
Behemoth is a punishment for sinners.
questions.correctAnswer: God made powerful creatures to coexist with humans.
questions.explanation: Job 40:15 says 'which I made with thee,' indicating God created the behemoth alongside humans, showing coexistence in creation.

questions.question: Job 40:8 asks if Job will disannul God's judgment. What does this imply about the attitude believers should have toward God's decisions?
options: Believers should trust and not condemn God's judgments.
Believers should question and override God's judgments.
Believers should only trust human judgment.
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should trust and not condemn God's judgments.
questions.explanation: Job 40:8 challenges Job’s questioning of God’s judgment, teaching believers to accept and trust divine decisions.

hard.title: Job Chapter 40 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Job Chapter 40.

questions.question: What does the behemoth's tail move like?
questions.correctAnswer: Like a cedar
questions.explanation: The behemoth's tail is compared to a cedar, indicating its strength and size (Job 40:17).

questions.question: What are the bones of the behemoth compared to?
questions.correctAnswer: Brass
questions.explanation: The bones are described as strong pieces of brass, emphasizing their durability (Job 40:18).

questions.question: Who is the behemoth described as in relation to God's creation?
questions.correctAnswer: The chief
questions.explanation: The behemoth is identified as the chief of the ways of God, signifying its importance in creation (Job 40:19).

questions.question: What do the mountains provide for the behemoth?
questions.correctAnswer: Food
questions.explanation: The verse states that the mountains bring forth food for the behemoth, where other beasts play (Job 40:20).

questions.question: Where does the behemoth lie?
questions.correctAnswer: Under shady trees
questions.explanation: The behemoth lies under shady trees, indicating its habitat (Job 40:21).

questions.question: What does the behemoth drink without haste?
questions.correctAnswer: A river
questions.explanation: The behemoth is described as drinking up a river without haste, demonstrating its size and strength (Job 40:23).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'behemoth' in Job 40:15 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Large creature
questions.explanation: 'Behemoth' in Hebrew signifies a large or mighty creature, particularly in the context of God's creation (Job 40:15).

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Job 40:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: The comparison of the behemoth's tail to a cedar is a simile, using 'like' to illustrate its strength (Job 40:17).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's sovereignty in creation as seen in Job 40:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Colossians 1:16
questions.explanation: Colossians 1:16 speaks of Christ's role in creation, echoing the sovereignty of God seen in Job 40:19.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of divine power displayed in Job 40:10-12?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 40:12
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:12 reflects on God's power in creation, paralleling the themes of divine authority in Job 40:10-12.

questions.question: What comes before Job 40:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Job 40:3
questions.explanation: Job 40:3 is the verse that directly precedes Job 40:4, where Job responds to God's challenge.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'his nose pierceth through snares' in Job 40:24?
questions.correctAnswer: He is powerful
questions.explanation: This phrase illustrates the behemoth's strength and ability to avoid traps, emphasizing its might (Job 40:24).

questions.question: The behemoth's ability to draw up the Jordan into its mouth signifies what about God's creation?
questions.correctAnswer: It is majestic
questions.explanation: The behemoth's grandeur in drawing rivers symbolizes the majesty of God's creation (Job 40:23).

questions.question: True or False: Job expresses confidence in his own righteousness in Job 40.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Job acknowledges his vileness and does not claim righteousness as he speaks to God (Job 40:4).

questions.question: True or False: The behemoth is depicted as a creature of great strength and power.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The descriptions of the behemoth showcase its immense strength and power throughout the chapter (Job 40:18-19).

theological.title: Job Chapter 40 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Job Chapter 40 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 40:2 teach about human limitations in relation to God's sovereignty?
options: Humans cannot instruct or correct God because His wisdom and sovereignty are absolute
Humans are equal partners with God in determining justice
God allows humans to reprove Him when they disagree with His actions
Humans have the authority to annul God's judgment when they are righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Humans cannot instruct or correct God because His wisdom and sovereignty are absolute
questions.explanation: Job 40:2 states, 'Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it,' demonstrating that humans do not possess the authority to instruct or correct God, highlighting His absolute sovereignty.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human repentance and humility is expressed in Job 40:4?
options: True repentance involves recognizing one's vileness and choosing silence before God
Repentance means arguing with God until one proves righteousness
Humility is unnecessary because God will justify human pride
Humans should persist in justifying themselves before God
questions.correctAnswer: True repentance involves recognizing one's vileness and choosing silence before God
questions.explanation: In Job 40:4, Job confesses, 'Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth,' illustrating true repentance as a humble acknowledgment of human unworthiness and a choice to remain silent before God's majesty.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice and human pride does Job 40:8 teach?
options: Human attempts to annul God's judgment are futile and often motivated by pride
Humans have the right to condemn God to establish their own righteousness
Divine justice is arbitrary and can be challenged by human reasoning
God requires human approval before executing judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Human attempts to annul God's judgment are futile and often motivated by pride
questions.explanation: Job 40:8 asks, 'Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?' indicating that human efforts to overturn divine justice are both presumptuous and rooted in pride.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 40:9 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Job 40:9 asks, 'Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?' highlighting God's omnipotence, emphasizing His unmatched power compared to humans.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 40:23 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty over creation
questions.explanation: Job 40:23 says, 'Behold, he drinketh up a river, and hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth,' illustrating God's sovereign control over even the mightiest creatures and waters.

questions.question: How does the depiction of Behemoth in Job 40:15–24 connect to the theme of God's creative power elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It prefigures the power of Christ as Creator in John 1
It contrasts with the chaos monsters defeated in Genesis 1
It illustrates God's authority over all creatures, affirming Psalm 104's praise of creation
It symbolizes the fall of Satan in Isaiah 14
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God's authority over all creatures, affirming Psalm 104's praise of creation
questions.explanation: The majestic description of Behemoth in Job 40:15–24 illustrates God's supreme authority over creation, aligning with Psalm 104's celebration of God's sovereign rule over all living beings.

questions.question: How does God's challenge to Job in Job 40:7–14 prepare for a fuller revelation of divine wisdom in later Scripture?
options: It anticipates the wisdom literature's emphasis on human humility before God
It foreshadows the New Testament teaching on justification by faith
It predicts the Mosaic law's focus on ritual purity
It prefigures the prophetic call for social justice exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the wisdom literature's emphasis on human humility before God
questions.explanation: God's challenge in Job 40:7–14 calling Job to gird up like a man but recognizing human limitations anticipates the broader wisdom tradition's focus on humility before God's inscrutable wisdom.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Job 40:8 and Job 40:9 teach about divine justice and power?
options: God's judgment is just because of His omnipotent power which humans cannot challenge
Human judgment is superior to divine power and should be heeded
God's justice is arbitrary and humans must explain it to be valid
Divine power is limited by human reasoning in matters of justice
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is just because of His omnipotent power which humans cannot challenge
questions.explanation: Job 40:8 questions human attempts to annul God's judgment, and 40:9 emphasizes God's unmatched power, together affirming that divine justice is grounded in God's omnipotence and is beyond human contestation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 40:4 and Job 40:14 teach about human righteousness and salvation?
options: True righteousness recognizes human inability to save oneself apart from God's power
Humans can save themselves by their own right hand
Salvation is achieved through human wisdom and judgment
Righteousness is attained by human contending with God
questions.correctAnswer: True righteousness recognizes human inability to save oneself apart from God's power
questions.explanation: Job 40:4 shows Job's acknowledgment of his vileness and silence, while 40:14 states God would confess if Job's own hand could save him, together teaching human salvation depends solely on God's power, not human effort.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 40:15 and Job 40:19 teach about God's providence in creation?
options: God's providence extends to the creation and sustenance of even the mightiest beasts
Behemoth is independent from God's control
God's providence is limited to humans only
Creation is chaotic and beyond God's ordering
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence extends to the creation and sustenance of even the mightiest beasts
questions.explanation: Job 40:15 introduces Behemoth as a creature God made with Job, and 40:19 calls him 'the chief of the ways of God,' affirming God's providential care over all creatures, no matter their might.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Job 40:7–14 teaches that human reason is irrelevant in understanding divine justice. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches that human reason is limited and must submit to God's sovereign judgment
It dismisses human reason entirely as worthless
It encourages humans to overthrow God's judgment using reason
It states that divine justice is unknowable and random
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that human reason is limited and must submit to God's sovereign judgment
questions.explanation: Job 40:7–14 involves God demanding Job to respond like a man but reminds him of his limitations, teaching that human reason is valid but subordinate to God's sovereign judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 40:3–5 teach about human repentance and the process of sanctification?
options: Sanctification involves confession of sin, restraint in speech, and submission to God's authority
Sanctification requires defending oneself against God
True sanctification is achieved through human effort alone
Repentance is unnecessary as God will justify all
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves confession of sin, restraint in speech, and submission to God's authority
questions.explanation: Job 40:3–5 records Job's admission of vileness, choosing silence, and ceasing to argue with God, which reflect stages of repentance and sanctification involving confession and submission.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 40:10 specifically demonstrate in the context of God's majesty?
questions.correctAnswer: Glory
questions.explanation: Job 40:10 commands to 'Deck thyself now with majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty,' focusing on the divine attribute of God's glory and majestic presence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 40:21 and Job 40:22 teach about God's provision and care for creation?
options: God provides suitable environments and protection for His creatures
Creation is left to survive by its own strength without God's care
God punishes all creatures equally without provision
The natural world is indifferent to God's will
questions.correctAnswer: God provides suitable environments and protection for His creatures
questions.explanation: Verses 40:21–22 describe Behemoth lying under shady trees and being covered by willows, symbolizing God's provision of habitat and protection within creation.

questions.question: How does Job 40:11–12 narratively contribute to the theme of God's justice and the fate of the proud in Scripture?
options: It portrays God's active subjugation and humiliation of the proud and wicked, consistent with Proverbs' warnings
It suggests the proud will ultimately triumph over God
It encourages pride as a path to righteousness
It implies that the wicked are protected from God's wrath
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays God's active subjugation and humiliation of the proud and wicked, consistent with Proverbs' warnings
questions.explanation: Job 40:11–12 commands to 'behold every one that is proud, and abase him,' narratively reinforcing the biblical theme, also found in Proverbs, that God brings down the proud and wicked.
